html:
Floods in July 2021 that struck western Germany, Belgium and the Netherlands after a slow moving storm dropped extreme rain over a few days. More than 200 people died.

The worst damage came in narrow valleys. In the Ahr valley in Germany small rivers rose many metres in hours and swept away houses, bridges and roads; most German deaths were there. In Belgium the Vesdre valley around Verviers and Liège was hit hard. Warnings existed, but they did not reach many people in time.

Scientists studying the event found that a warmer climate made such heavy rain more likely and more intense, and the floods became a European symbol of climate change arriving close to home. They also showed how much the danger of floods had been forgotten in places far from the sea, unlike the coastal Netherlands after the North Sea flood of 1953.
sum: Floods in July 2021 that struck western Germany, Belgium and the Netherlands after a slow moving storm dropped extreme rain over a few days. More than 200 people died.
